title: English Level Placement Test
description: Find your starting point - 15 minute assessment

instructions.overview: This test will help us find the right starting point for you. It has 4 sections: Grammar, Listening, Reading, and Speaking. Answer honestly - this helps us give you the best learning experience!
rules: Take your time - there's no time limit
Answer as many questions as you can
It's okay to skip questions you don't know
Use a quiet place for the listening and speaking sections
You need a microphone for the speaking section

sections.title: Section 1: Grammar & Vocabulary
sections.description: Choose the best answer for each question

questions.question: My name ___ Ahmed.
She ___ from Somalia.
I ___ two brothers.
He ___ at a hospital.
Do you ___ English?
I ___ to the store yesterday.
She has ___ in Portland for three years.
If I ___ more money, I would buy a car.
The book ___ by millions of people.
I wish I ___ speak Spanish fluently.
By next year, I ___ studying English for five years.
The project should ___ by the end of the month.
She insisted ___ going alone.
Neither the students nor the teacher ___ ready.
Had I known about the meeting, I ___ attended.

sections.title: Section 2: Listening Comprehension
sections.description: Listen to each audio clip and answer the question

questions.transcript: My name is Sarah. I am 25 years old. I live in Portland.
questions.question: What is the speaker's name?

questions.transcript: I work at a hospital. I am a nurse. I help sick people.
questions.question: Where does the speaker work?

questions.transcript: Last weekend, I went to the park with my family. We had a picnic and played soccer. It was very fun.
questions.question: What did the speaker do last weekend?

questions.transcript: I've been studying English for two years now. At first, it was really difficult, but I'm making progress. My goal is to speak fluently by next year.
questions.question: How long has the speaker been studying English?

questions.transcript: The economic implications of the policy shift remain unclear. While proponents argue it will stimulate growth, critics contend that the potential risks outweigh the benefits, particularly for vulnerable populations.
questions.question: What is the main concern of the critics?

sections.title: Section 3: Reading Comprehension
sections.description: Read each passage and answer the questions

passages.title: A New Life in America
passages.text: Ahmed moved to Portland last year. He came from Somalia with his family. At first, everything was very difficult. He didn't speak English well. He couldn't find a job. But Ahmed didn't give up. He started taking English classes at the community college. He practiced every day. Now, one year later, Ahmed speaks English much better. He has a job at a grocery store. He is happy in his new home.

questions.question: Where did Ahmed come from?
What was difficult for Ahmed at first?
Where does Ahmed work now?
How does Ahmed feel now?

passages.title: The Digital Divide
passages.text: The rapid advancement of technology has created a significant gap between those who have access to digital resources and those who do not. This phenomenon, known as the digital divide, affects educational opportunities, economic mobility, and social participation. While urban areas often benefit from high-speed internet and modern devices, rural communities frequently lack these essential tools. Addressing this disparity requires coordinated efforts from government, private sector, and community organizations to ensure equitable access to technology for all citizens.

questions.question: What is the 'digital divide'?
options: The gap in access to technology

questions.question: According to the passage, who is most affected by the digital divide?
What does the passage suggest is needed to solve this problem?

prompts.prompt: Introduce yourself. Say your name, where you are from, and one thing about yourself.
prompts.example: My name is Ahmed. I am from Somalia. I like to play soccer.

prompts.prompt: Describe your daily routine. What do you do in the morning? What do you do in the evening?
prompts.example: In the morning, I wake up at 7 AM. I eat breakfast and go to work. In the evening, I come home and watch TV.

prompts.prompt: What are your goals for learning English? How will speaking English help you in your life?
prompts.example: I want to learn English to get a better job. Speaking English will help me communicate with more people and have more opportunities.

levels.description: You are just starting to learn English
levels.message: Welcome! You'll start with basic conversations and survival English. Don't worry - we'll guide you every step of the way!
Great! You have a good foundation. We'll start with practical topics like work, shopping, and daily life situations.

levels.description: You can communicate in most everyday situations
levels.message: Excellent! You can handle everyday conversations. We'll help you express opinions and have deeper discussions.

levels.description: You can express yourself fluently in most situations
levels.message: Impressive! You speak English well. We'll focus on academic skills and writing to prepare you for advanced work or study.
Outstanding! Your English is very strong. We'll focus on advanced academic skills and ACT preparation.
